facts.fact: Congressional campaigns typically spend between $500,000 and $5 million or more on TV advertising, depending on district competitiveness and media market costs.
facts.quote: Congressional campaigns typically spend between $500,000 and $5 million or more on TV advertising, depending on the competitiveness of the district and media market costs.

facts.fact: State legislature races generally require $50,000 to $500,000 in TV spending.
facts.quote: State legislature races generally require $50,000 to $500,000 in TV spending, while county-wide races like county commissioner or sheriff typically need $25,000 to $200,000.

facts.fact: County-wide races such as county commissioner or sheriff typically need $25,000 to $200,000 in TV advertising spending.
facts.quote: county-wide races like county commissioner or sheriff typically need $25,000 to $200,000.

facts.fact: Local races such as city council or school board can be effective with $5,000 to $50,000 in TV advertising.
facts.quote: Local races such as city council or school board can be effective with $5,000 to $50,000 in TV advertising.

facts.fact: Media typically represents 40-60% of total campaign spending.
facts.quote: with media typically representing 40-60% of total campaign spending.

facts.fact: The page recommends allocating 10-15% of the TV budget to early-campaign name recognition (6+ months out).
facts.quote: Early campaign (6+ months out):** 10-15% of budget for name recognition

facts.fact: The page recommends allocating 25-35% of budget to mid-campaign persuasion messaging.
facts.quote: Mid-campaign:** 25-35% for persuasion messaging

facts.fact: The page recommends allocating 50-60% of budget to the final 4-6 weeks for peak advertising and GOTV.
facts.quote: Final 4-6 weeks:** 50-60% for peak advertising and GOTV

facts.fact: Political ad rates can increase 3-5x during peak demand periods as election day approaches.
facts.quote: political ad rates](https://adwave.com/resources/political-ad-rates-2026) can increase 3-5x during peak demand periods.

facts.fact: Federal candidates are entitled to the lowest unit rate stations charge for comparable ad time during specific pre-election windows.
facts.quote: Federal candidates are entitled to the lowest rate stations charge for comparable ad time during specific pre-election windows

facts.fact: A typical channel allocation suggests 50-60% of the TV budget to broadcast TV.
facts.quote: A typical allocation might dedicate 50-60% of the TV budget to broadcast for broad reach, credibility, and live event coverage.

facts.fact: A typical channel allocation suggests 15-25% of the TV budget to cable TV.
facts.quote: Cable typically receives 15-25% of the budget to reach targeted audiences and news viewers.

facts.fact: A typical channel allocation suggests 20-30% of the TV budget to CTV and streaming.
facts.quote: CTV and streaming should receive 20-30% of the budget to reach cord-cutters with precise targeting capabilities.

facts.fact: 15-second and 30-second spots are standard political ad lengths, with 60-second spots used for fundraising or complex messages.
facts.quote: 15-second and 30-second spots are standard. 60-second spots for fundraising or complex messages.

facts.fact: Recommended minimum video format for political TV ads is HD at 1920x1080.
facts.quote: HD video (1920x1080 minimum)

facts.fact: The page states that CTV platforms allow campaigns to start with budgets as low as $50-100 per day.
facts.quote: CTV platforms allow campaigns to start with budgets as low as $50-100 per day.

facts.fact: The page advises starting name recognition advertising 4-6 months before election day for competitive races.
facts.quote: Start name recognition advertising 4-6 months before election day for competitive races.

facts.fact: The page says smaller races may begin TV advertising 2-3 months before election day.
facts.quote: Smaller races may begin 2-3 months out.

facts.fact: The page states voters need to see a political message 7-10 times to remember it.
facts.quote: Voters need to see your message 7-10 times to remember it.
